```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
# The benchmarking section uses the suggested package tempdisagg
has_tempdisagg <- requireNamespace("tempdisagg", quietly = TRUE)
```

```{r setup}
library(chainlink)
```

This vignette follows a complete workflow, from raw quarterly data to the series
that are usually published: chain-linked volume series, growth rates and
contributions to growth. It does not require to know the examples of the IMF
manual (see the vignette `imf_qna_manual` for them).

The data are those of the example 8.2 of the manual: two products, `A` and `B`,
with their current prices and their price indices over the previous year
(2010 is the reference year).

# 1. Prepare the inputs

The functions use `ts` objects. Raw data usually come as a table, with one row per
quarter:

```{r raw}
raw <- data.frame(
	year = rep(2010:2013, each = 4),
	quarter = rep(1:4, times = 4),
	A_cp = as.numeric(data8.2cp[, "A"]),
	B_cp = as.numeric(data8.2cp[, "B"]),
	A_pi = as.numeric(data8.2ep[, "A"]),
	B_pi = as.numeric(data8.2ep[, "B"])
)
head(raw, 6)
```

```{r to-ts}
to_ts <- function(df, columns, names) {
	res <- ts(as.matrix(df[, columns]),
			  start = c(df$year[1], df$quarter[1]), frequency = 4)
	colnames(res) <- names
	res
}
cp <- to_ts(raw, c("A_cp", "B_cp"), c("A", "B"))
price_idx <- to_ts(raw, c("A_pi", "B_pi"), c("A", "B"))
```

What the functions expect:

* `cp`: current prices of the components, without the total. They must cover the
  reference year (2010 here), whose annual sum gives the level of the chain
  measures;
* `price_idx`: price indices over the previous year (average of the previous
  year = 100). They are not needed in the reference year (here they are
  missing in 2010).

```{r check-inputs}
window(price_idx, end = c(2011, 2))
```

If the price indices are given over the previous quarter (or month) instead,
the quarter-to-quarter indices of `fisher()` or `laspeyres()` need
`reference_freq = 4`, and `pi_py2pp()` converts price indices over the previous
year to indices over the previous quarter.

# 2. Chain-linked volume series

With the annual overlap technique and 2010 as reference year, the chain-linked
Laspeyres-type volume measures (in monetary terms) of the products and of
their total are:

```{r chain}
x <- chain_laspeyres(cp, price_idx, method = "ao", base_year = 2010,
					 output = "measure")
round(x, 1)
```

The last column is the total. Chain volume measures are not additive: the
total differs from the sum of the products, except in 2010 and 2011.

```{r discrepancy}
chain_discrepancy(x) |> round(2)
```

The same series as indices (2010 = 100):

```{r index}
idx <- chain_laspeyres(cp, price_idx, method = "ao", base_year = 2010,
					   output = "index")
round(idx, 2)
```

# 3. Growth rates and contributions

Growth rates of the total, over the previous quarter and over the same quarter of
the previous year:

```{r growth}
growth_qoq <- 100 * (x[, "Total"] / stats::lag(x[, "Total"], -1) - 1)
growth_yoy <- 100 * (x[, "Total"] / stats::lag(x[, "Total"], -4) - 1)
round(ts.union(`Quarter-to-quarter` = growth_qoq, `Year-on-year` = growth_yoy), 2)
```

Contributions of the products to these growth rates. `chain_contrib()` takes the
output of `chain_laspeyres()` and the current prices of the components; `extra`
adds the growth of the total and the residual (growth minus the sum of the
contributions):

```{r contrib}
contrib_qoq <- chain_contrib(x, cp, method = "ao", type = "period",
							 extra = c("total", "residual"))
contrib_yoy <- chain_contrib(x, cp, method = "ao", type = "yoy",
							 extra = c("total", "residual"))
round(contrib_qoq, 3)
round(contrib_yoy, 3)
```

The residual is zero if the data are fully consistent. Here it is not exactly
zero (the annual price indices of the example are not exactly consistent with the
quarterly data) but it is negligible: it must be reported rather than allocated.

```{r residual}
max(abs(contrib_qoq[, "Residual"]), na.rm = TRUE)
max(abs(contrib_yoy[, "Residual"]), na.rm = TRUE)
```

# 4. A chart for the publication

Stacked contributions and growth of the total (year-on-year):

```{r chart, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
plot_contributions <- function(contrib, main) {
	comp <- as.matrix(contrib[, c("A", "B")])
	growth <- as.numeric(contrib[, "Total"])
	labels <- paste0(floor(time(contrib)), "Q", cycle(contrib))
	keep <- !is.na(comp[, 1])
	bp <- barplot(t(comp[keep, ]), names.arg = labels[keep],
				  col = c("grey35", "grey75"), las = 2, cex.names = 0.7,
				  ylab = "Percentage points", main = main)
	lines(bp, growth[keep], type = "b", pch = 19)
	legend("topleft", legend = c("A", "B", "Total"),
		   fill = c("grey35", "grey75", NA), border = c("black", "black", NA),
		   pch = c(NA, NA, 19), lty = c(NA, NA, 1), bty = "n")
}
plot_contributions(contrib_yoy, "Contributions to year-on-year growth")
```

# 5. Annual series and change of the reference year

Contributions to the growth of the annual sums:

```{r annual}
chain_contrib(x, cp, method = "ao", type = "annual", extra = "total") |>
	round(3)
```

Indices are often published with a recent reference year. `chain_rebase()` changes
it (the average of the new year is 100) without changing the growth rates:

```{r rebase}
chain_rebase(idx, base_year = 2012) |> round(2)
```

The contributions must be computed from the measures built with their original
reference year (here 2010), before rebasing.

# 6. One-quarter overlap and benchmarking

With the one-quarter overlap technique, the quarterly series are linked on the last
quarter of the year, so that the annual sums of the chain volume measures differ
from those of the annual chain series (annual overlap). They can be benchmarked
on them with the `tempdisagg` package (Denton, Cholette's variant), as in the
vignette `imf_qna_manual`.

```{r oqo}
x_oqo <- chain_laspeyres(cp, price_idx, method = "oqo", base_year = 2010,
						 output = "measure")
contrib_oqo <- chain_contrib(x_oqo, cp, method = "oqo", type = "yoy", pi = price_idx,
							 extra = c("total", "residual"))
round(contrib_oqo, 3)
```

```{r benchmark, eval = has_tempdisagg}
annual_ao <- aggregate(x[, "Total"], FUN = sum)
x_oqo_total <- x_oqo[, "Total"]
bench <- tempdisagg::td(annual_ao ~ 0 + x_oqo_total,
						conversion = "sum", method = "denton-cholette")
x_oqo_bench <- predict(bench)
ts.union(`One-quarter overlap` = x_oqo_total,
		 `Benchmarked` = x_oqo_bench) |> round(1)
```

The contributions above are those of the non-benchmarked one-quarter overlap
series: benchmarking the total alone breaks the link between the total and its
components, so the contributions of the benchmarked series are not available
through `chain_contrib()`.

# 7. Seasonal adjustment of chain-linked series

Chain-linked volume series are often seasonally adjusted. The ESS Guidelines on
Seasonal Adjustment (item 5.6) describe how to derive the seasonally adjusted
aggregate of annually chain-linked Laspeyres-type components **indirectly**, that
is by aggregating the seasonally adjusted components:

1. seasonally adjust the chain volume measures of the components;
2. un-chain them (`chain_unchain()`): the volume at the prices of the previous year
   is additive within each year;
3. aggregate them and chain-link the aggregate again, with the same technique;
4. re-reference it to the reference year (the annual current prices of the
   reference year are those of the unadjusted data).

`chain_aggregate()` does the steps 2 to 4. Here the seasonal adjustment is an
illustration with `stats::stl()` (the data of the example only have 12 quarters
and no real seasonality, so that the adjustment is not meaningful in itself):

```{r sa-stl}
sa_stl <- function(s) {
	fit <- stats::stl(s, s.window = "periodic")
	fit$time.series[, "trend"] + fit$time.series[, "remainder"]
}
# Step 1: seasonally adjusted chain volume measures of the components
x_sa <- ts.union(A = sa_stl(x[, "A"]), B = sa_stl(x[, "B"]))
round(x_sa, 1)
```

Step 2: un-chained components, i.e. volumes at the prices of the previous year,
that can be summed:

```{r sa-unchain}
chain_unchain(x_sa, cp, base_year = 2010) |> round(1)
```

Steps 3 and 4: the indirectly seasonally adjusted aggregate, compared to the direct
adjustment of the aggregate and to the unadjusted data:

```{r sa-aggregate}
indirect <- chain_aggregate(x_sa, cp, base_year = 2010, output = "measure")
direct <- sa_stl(x[, "Total"])
sa <- ts.union(Unadjusted = x[, "Total"], `SA direct` = direct,
			   `SA indirect` = indirect)
round(sa, 1)
```

The two approaches give different seasonally adjusted aggregates. The annual
totals of the seasonally adjusted series are not forced to be those of the
unadjusted data:

```{r sa-annual}
aggregate(sa, FUN = sum) |> round(1)
```

If users require it and if the unadjusted data are additive, the guidelines
suggest forcing the annual totals (for instance with the Denton method of the
`tempdisagg` package, as in the vignette on the manual). The indirect approach
only exists for Laspeyres-type series: for the other chain-linked indices, only
the direct approach is feasible. With the one-quarter overlap technique, use
`method = "oqo"` and the price indices `pi` (the overlap quarter is valued at the
average prices of the year).
